external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the supplier document portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.
external_entities.notes: The text does not place suppliers in a trust zone.

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded compliance paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the supplier document portal, issues supplier credentials, and pushes a nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
external_entities.notes: The text does not place the vendor entity itself in a trust zone.

processes.name: Supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
processes.notes: The vendor datasheet claims the platform is secure by design, uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, fully authenticates and audits access, and is fully compliant.

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: A service in our cloud account that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes the records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor's platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where the uploaded compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_stores.notes: The vendor datasheet claims enterprise-grade encryption throughout.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A landing bucket in our cloud account receiving the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a landing bucket in our cloud account
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The supplier database in our cloud account into which the supplier master service writes extracted records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it in the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection status.

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The supplier document portal stores the uploaded documents in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: Conflicting claims about the extract: System description says, 'We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end.' The same source says, 'The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.'

data_flows.name: load file
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes extracted supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract.

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor's platform
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled platform hosting the supplier document portal and retaining uploaded documents.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: Our cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it a portal; the extraction procedure defines a portal as a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor's platform is a tenant trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source says the portal is a SaaS product hosted by the vendor and that we do not run any part of it.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate network is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source names the corporate network as the location from which category managers work; no distinct authority difference is stated.

assumptions.assumption: Our cloud account is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source places the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database in our cloud account; no distinct authority difference is stated.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's data classification is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details, which are personal and commercially sensitive records.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's data classification is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The bucket stores a supplier data extract containing supplier records and staff contact details.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's data classification is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The database stores supplier records from the extract, including contact details for staff.
